title: Open-loop and closed-loop op-amp frequency response

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
An op-amp's open-loop gain \(A(j\omega)\) is huge at DC and falls past its dominant pole. Well above that pole, it behaves like an integrator: \(A \approx \omega_u/(j\omega)\), with a constant \(-90^\circ\) phase.

Closing the loop trades that gain for bandwidth. The closed-loop response is flat at about \(1/f\) and has its own single pole where the open-loop curve meets it, at \(f\,\omega_u\). On a Bode plot you can read it graphically: draw the flat line at \(1/f\) in dB, and the closed-loop corner is where it hits the open-loop \(-20\) dB/decade line. The closed-loop step response is then a simple exponential with that time constant.
sections.figure_alt: Small input step and an exponential output.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ A(j\omega) = \frac{A_0}{1 + j\omega/\omega_{-3dB}} \approx \frac{\omega_u}{j\omega}\ \ (\omega \gg \omega_{-3dB}) \]
\[ A_{CL}(j\omega) = \frac{A}{1 + Af} \approx \frac{1/f}{1 + j\omega/(f\omega_u)} \]
Closed-loop step: \(v_o(t) = \frac{V}{f}\left(1 - e^{-t\,f\omega_u}\right)\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
An op-amp has \(\omega_u = 2\pi\times8\ \mathrm{MHz}\) and is used at closed-loop gain 4 (\(f = 0.25\)).
\[ \omega_{CL} = 0.25\times2\pi\times8\ \mathrm{MHz} = 2\pi\times2\ \mathrm{MHz} \]
The closed-loop time constant is \(1/\omega_{CL} \approx 80\ \mathrm{ns}\), so a small step settles to 1% in about \(4.6\times80 \approx 370\ \mathrm{ns}\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Thinking phase is \(-45^\circ\) everywhere above the pole; that is only at the pole.
- Expecting a single-pole op-amp to reach \(-180^\circ\).
- Using closed-loop gain in dB where a linear ratio is needed.
- Applying the small-signal bandwidth to large steps that slew.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Small-signal bandwidth is only half the speed story. Large signals hit the slew-rate limit, which is the next skill. Always check which limit binds first, the small-signal bandwidth or the slew rate.
